status: Contract-milestone freeze for the 0.3.0-preview.1 packages (architecture D14, report §18). The two dependency ceilings that existed before (180,000 and 250,000 bytes gzip) are unchanged; the lazy-asset and content ceilings are first freezes set from the measurement recorded in docs/study-harness/evidence/consumer.json with stated headroom. Raising any ceiling needs a recorded decision with the new measurement and its user impact (docs/study-harness/performance.md §5).

compression.library: node:zlib gzipSync over the exact emitted file bytes
compression.gzipDefault: zlib default level (Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION = 6), the level scripts/verify-packages.mjs has always used
compression.woff2: font files are already compressed; their budgets are raw bytes

legacy2dConsumer.rule: Sum over every emitted dist/assets/*.js file of gzipSync(bytes) at the zlib default level, exactly as scripts/verify-packages.mjs measures it. Includes React, ReactDOM, @explorable-models/core/declarative, @explorable-models/player, the @explorable-models/agent document tools and the document worker of both entries.
legacy2dConsumer.forbidden: No Three.js, Playwright or MCP SDK code in any emitted JS (text markers THREE.REVISION, WebGLRenderer, playwright-core, @modelcontextprotocol).
measurements: scripts/verify-packages.mjs from the release/preview tarballs (core, activity, player, agent)
scripts/study-harness/verify-consumer.mjs: the same consumer rebuilt inside the six-package clean install (re-measure with the same rule)

activityEntry.consumer: examples/study-harness-consumer (production Vite build inside the clean install of the six packed tarballs)
activityEntry.rule: Sum of gzip9 sizes of every .js file statically reachable from the entry HTML: the HTML's <script type="module" src> and <link rel="modulepreload"> files, their transitive static imports (import-statement edges of an esbuild metafile over the emitted files), and every .js file referenced with new URL('…', import.meta.url) from those files (the catalogue kernel module worker) together with its static imports. It therefore includes React, ReactDOM, the activity runtime, the installed catalogue's eager index and review authority, the learner surface, the consumer's host code and the kernel worker.
activityEntry.excludes: Targets of dynamic import() and their closures, from the page and from the kernel worker: the KaTeX chunk, @explorable-models/player-3d and Three.js, the per-template catalogue content chunks fetched by createLazyCatalog().load(), the per-kernel modules the catalogue worker loads on first use (INSTALLED_KERNEL_SOURCE), optional capture-rendering and saved-record migration implementations reached only by their asynchronous operations, and the KaTeX font URL table requested only by visible math with bundled fonts. Their emitted raw/gzip bytes are reported individually in consumer evidence (lazy.other); the asset ceilings below still apply to math, 3D and catalogue content. CSS, fonts and source maps are not JS and are not counted here.
activityEntry.note: Unchanged rule and ceiling. The Phase 4a measurement (281,836 B plain DOM, 280,246 B React) exceeded the ceiling (performance.md F1); the cause was fixed, not re-budgeted: the consumer uses the on-demand catalogue (content per template on demand, verified against the installed index), the catalogue worker loads kernel code per kernel on first use and the schema 2.0 document compiler is opt-in (enableDocumentExecution), so neither reaches a kernel-only page or worker.

forbiddenInEagerGraph.rule: No source of an eager chunk (from its hidden source map) may come from: three, @explorable-models/player-3d, katex (or the player's bundled KaTeX chunk), playwright / playwright-core / @playwright, @modelcontextprotocol, provider SDKs (openai, @anthropic-ai, @google/generative-ai, @google/genai, @mistralai, cohere-ai, ollama, @aws-sdk/client-bedrock*), @tauri-apps, @explorable-models/cli or @explorable-models/agent; no eager JS may contain the text markers THREE.REVISION, WebGLRenderer, "KaTeX parse error", playwright-core or @modelcontextprotocol; the entry HTML has no inline script.

lazyMath.freeze: First freeze: KaTeX 0.19.0 as bundled by @explorable-models/player and minified by the consumer's Vite build, measured 259,208 B (76,670 B gzip9) JS, 24,793 B (3,518 B gzip9) CSS and 259,792 B of fonts on 2026-10-26; ceilings are those measurements plus about 10 % headroom, rounded.
lazyMath.rule: KaTeX code reached only through the learner surface's default mathLoader (dynamic import), the KaTeX stylesheet fetched when math first renders, and the KaTeX woff2 fonts (registered only with fonts: 'bundled'; a browser downloads only the faces it uses).

bundledUiFonts.freeze: First freeze from 152,320 B measured (three Inter variable subsets) plus about 10 % headroom.
bundledUiFonts.rule: Inter woff2 subsets (greek, latin-ext, latin) emitted for fonts: 'bundled'; the default fonts: 'system' loads none.

lazy3d.freeze: First freeze from 615,373 B (157,110 B gzip9) measured for player-3d with three 0.186.1, plus about 10 % headroom.
lazy3d.rule: Every .js file reachable from a dynamic import() whose source map includes @explorable-models/player-3d or three: the renderer loaded through the host's spatialLoader. Never fetched by a 2D template.

catalogueContent.freeze: First freeze from 158,169 B measured for the five installed packages plus about 10 % headroom. This is a record of content size, not a relaxation of the activity-entry ceiling.
catalogueContent.rule: Uncompressed bytes that the source maps of the single-page plain-DOM activity build attribute to @explorable-models/catalog templates/, copy/, models/ and content/<template-id> (activity templates, learner copy, model manifests): the eager graph must carry none of it (content is loaded per template on demand by createLazyCatalog), the main thread no kernel code, and the content of all five installed templates in its lazy chunks, together, at most maxBytes. Kernel modules (loaded by the catalogue worker on first use) and the kernel constants that templates and manifests reuse (IDs, versions, domains) are reported per chunk in the evidence.

performance.referenceMachine: The machine recorded in docs/study-harness/evidence/performance.json (userAgent, hardwareConcurrency, OS, CPU). Targets are engineering targets for that machine. scripts/study-harness/benchmark.mjs measures them in Chromium; the native conformance run's `performance` chain (examples/study-harness-tauri/scripts/performance-targets.mjs) measures the ones that apply to a host (input feedback, 2D preview, commit to visible frame, suspension, lifecycle, spatial orbit input) in the packaged reference host's WKWebView on the machine recorded in docs/study-harness/evidence/native-conformance.json, against these same targets. They are not low-end-device or whole-application guarantees.
performance.build: Production consumer build from scripts/study-harness/verify-consumer.mjs (release/study-harness/consumer/dist) served with the production CSP.
performance.statistics: Nearest-rank p50/p95 and max with the sample count, after warmup samples that are discarded.

inputFeedbackAck.measure: input event timeStamp of a real pointer drag on a slider → paint of the first frame whose control output shows that value (or a later one)

preview2d.packagedScopeDecision: Report §18 scope decision, 2026-10-28: support the existing usable 30 fps floor for the ordinary quadratic drag in the macOS reference host's WKWebView; retain 60 fps as an explicitly unmet improvement objective, not a packaged guarantee. Full packaged runs full-2026-10-27T04:20:05.108Z and full-2026-10-27T07:14:12.490Z measured 56.03 and 58.56 fps respectively (the latter 32 dropped of 695 display frames). These repeated packaged measurements do not establish a stable 60 fps path; further profiling/optimization is deferred rather than represented as complete. Input acknowledgement, scientific agreement, newest-frame handling, the 90% tentative/input cadence rule, dependency budgets and the 100 ms commit target are unchanged. User impact: occasional missed display frames on the packaged drag, with the same exact-entry alternative and canonical scientific state. This scope does not apply to other platforms or the separate Chromium benchmark; see performance.md §3b and architecture.md D14.
preview2d.measure: requestAnimationFrame cadence during a scripted 60 Hz slider drag (dropped frames counted against the idle refresh interval) and the rate of distinct tentative frames painted

commitToVisibleFrame.scope: small 2D workloads (catalogue 2D activities and the legacy document wave preset)
commitToVisibleFrame.measure: command call → paint of the first frame whose DOM shows the new committed frame; worker evaluation, render and storage acknowledgement reported separately

offscreen.measure: suspended history cards during a quiet window: 0 worker messages, 0 DOM mutations, 0 projection notifications, no timers or animation frames attributable to them

lifecycle.measure: workers, timers, intervals, window/document/MediaQueryList listeners, shadow roots/surfaces and open activities after 100 mount/interact/suspend/save/dispose/restore/mount/suspend/resume/dispose cycles: activity-owned counts return to zero; the bounded worker pool is identified separately

performance.hostLevelNotLibraryGuarantees: The report's 3-second cached launch and approximately 250 MB idle / 500 MB ordinary-study memory targets are whole-application targets for the host (Study Harness); this library does not measure or guarantee them.
